subject: beaver parachute
title: What If You Parachuted Beavers Into the Wilderness? Idaho Dropped 76

scenes.text: What if you moved beavers by dropping them out of a plane? Idaho did, in 1948.
After the war, people moved in around Payette Lake, and the local beavers kept felling trees and building dams.
Hauling them out overland failed. The pack horses and mules spooked, and the beavers overheated in their crates.
So a Fish and Game officer, Elmo Heter, took surplus army parachutes and designed a wooden box that springs open on landing.
His test jumper was an older male named Geronimo, dropped again and again, until he started crawling back into the box by himself.
That year, 76 beavers floated down into the remote Chamberlain Basin. All but one survived, and within weeks there were signs of new dams. The footage sat forgotten until 2015.

description:
What if you relocated beavers by parachute? In 1948 the Idaho Department of Fish and Game dropped 76 of them into the remote Chamberlain Basin in wooden boxes built to spring open on landing, using surplus wartime parachutes.
The idea came from Elmo Heter after overland moves with horses and mules went badly; a beaver named Geronimo made the test drops. All but one survived, and film of the operation resurfaced in 2015.

first_comment: Geronimo was dropped so often that he started crawling back into his box by himself. Which animal would you never put in a parachute?
